title: openai-compat: support Responses API variants + seed/determinism and metadata passthrough
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Add support for OpenAI Responses API variants, seed/determinism passthrough, and metadata passthrough; update SDK shims and docs; improve streaming stability and structured tool-calling compatibility.
description:
Motivation: OpenAI's Responses API introduces several variant response shapes (output vs choices fields), and exposes seed/determinism controls and arbitrary metadata passed through. Existing OpenAI compatibility layer in Redwood assumed the older completions/chat shapes and dropped upstream metadata and seed/determinism flags in several codepaths.

This PR implements a compatibility adapter that: 1) normalizes Responses API variants into Redwood's internal response model (supports both 'output' arrays and legacy 'choices'), 2) preserves and forwards seed/determinism flags from the OpenAI-compat request to the serving runtime (so deterministic runs and seeding experiments behave as users expect), 3) passes through user-provided metadata from the openai-style request payload into response objects and the audit logs, and 4) addresses a streaming stability edge-case when transitioning between output chunks and structured tool-calling events.

What changed (high-level): consolidated response adapter logic under redwood/openai_compat/response_adapter.py; added deterministic_seed plumbing in the request -> runtime layer; preserved metadata across the compatibility shim and included it in audit traces and per-token metrics; improved streamer boundary handling to avoid truncated structured output events; updated SDK shim (python) to expose new fields; added compatibility and integration tests; docs updated with examples and migration notes.

Testing and rollout: added unit tests and an integration test that exercises Responses variants with seed and metadata passthrough. CI initially exposed a flaky streaming test which was fixed by adjusting the streamer chunk buffer semantics and adding a small backpressure/read loop in the adapter. This was validated on canary host before merging.

Notes: no breaking API changes for existing Redwood users; this is additive to the OpenAI-compat surface and recommended for customers using Responses or experimenting with determinism/seeding.

Related: ENG-4821, ENG-4890, PM-211.

Checklist:
- [x] Response adapter for both 'output' and 'choices' shapes
- [x] Seed/determinism passthrough to runtime
- [x] Metadata passthrough to responses and audit logs
- [x] Streaming stability fix for structured events
- [x] SDK shim updates and docs
- [x] Tests (unit + integration)
commits_summary: feat(openai-compat): add response_adapter that normalizes 'output' and 'choices' shapes
fix(streaming): stabilize chunk boundary handling to prevent truncated structured events
feat(runtime): thread deterministic_seed through request context to the runtime scheduler
test(openai-compat): add tests for metadata passthrough and seed determinism
docs(openai-compat): document Responses variant compatibility and migration notes
diff_snippets: response_adapter.py: normalize_responses() handles both payload.get('output') and payload.get('choices') and maps to internal .outputs list
streamer.py: flush_chunk() now ensures structured marker is emitted when switching event types to avoid partial JSON chunks
runtime request flow: request.context['deterministic_seed'] populated from compat layer when present
sdk-python shim: openai_responses() accepts seed and metadata kwargs and forwards them unmodified
docs: migration example showing using 'seed' param and verifying metadata received in audit logs
